title: Genomics invoice versus installation correspondence
question: Do the February 2015 software invoice and June 2015 server email establish delivery or operation?
findingA: The February invoice requests $30,000 for analysis software and services involving gene-expression/SNP data, installation and training.
findingB: The June email reports that software could not yet be installed remotely because router access had not been configured.
sharedContext: Both records discuss AI-related software and infrastructure within the broader Southern Trust/Novamente research context.
notEstablished: They do not identify a shared server asset, show invoice settlement, confirm installation, or prove that a genetic-data platform operated.
alternative: The server may have belonged to a separate experiment or an installation attempt that never reached production.
nextCheck: Locate vendor acceptance, server asset IDs, signed scope, delivery confirmation and independent transaction records.

title: 2013 estate-planning draft versus 2014 algorithms invoice
question: Did the 2013 draft and the July 2014 algorithms invoice cover the same engagement?
findingA: A revised February 2013 draft describes conditional estate-planning fees totaling $23.5 million.
findingB: The July 2014 invoice document describes $20 million in algorithms for estate planning and has an unfilled billed-entity placeholder.
sharedContext: The documents name Southern Trust and Leon Black and refer to estate planning, but dates, sums and documentary form differ.
notEstablished: An executed agreement, amendment linking these documents, settled payment or software delivery is not established.
alternative: They may be different proposals, revised scopes, unrelated billing phases or incomplete drafts.
nextCheck: Seek an executed agreement, amendment identifying both documents, final invoice, settlement records and accepted deliverables. Do not sum the figures.
